answers.answer_text: To go abroad, to leave one's country.
To assume, to take up a job or post.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What does dānrèn lǐngdǎo gōngzuò mean?

answers.answer_text: To take on leadership work, to take up a leading post.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Translate into English: Nǐ zài zhèr dānrèn shénme gōngzuò?

answers.answer_text: What is your job title here?

questions_and_answers.question_text: Translate into Chinese: In what year did he go abroad?
Translate into Chinese: Some of them have to take up leading posts in technical fields.
Write a Chinese sentence using dānrèn with a post or office.
Explain the literal make-up of the phrase dānrèn lǐngdǎo gōngzuò.
Translate into Chinese: Are there many women among the graduate students who go abroad to study?

articles.text:
7. A: Nǐmende yánjiūshēng chū guó xuéxí yǐhòu dōu huí dàxué jiāo shū ma?
   After going abroad to study, do all your graduate students go back to the universities and teach?
   B: Bù. Yǒu yíbùfen děi dānrèn jìshu fāngmiànde lǐngdǎo gōngzuò.
   No. Some of them have to take up leading posts in technical fields.

Notes on No. 7

chū guó: "to go abroad"

Tā shi něinián chū guóde?
In what year did he go abroad?

Chū guó liúxuéde yánjiūshēng nǚde duō bu duō?
Are there many women among the graduate students who go abroad to study?

dānrèn: "to assume," "to take up" a job or post

Nǐ zài zhèr dānrèn shénme gōngzuò?
What is your job title here?

Tā zuìjìn yào qù Ōuzhōu dānrèn lǐngshì gōngzuò.
He will soon be going to Europe to do consular work.

Tā dānrènguo Měidàsī sīzhǎng.
He has been the chief of the Department of American and Oceanic Affairs.

Dānrèn lǐngdǎo gōngzuò, as in sentence 7B, is an often used phrase for "to take on leadership work," "to take up a leading post" (that is, to be in a job in which one is in charge of others).
